statement: If there be as many numbers as we please in continued proportion, and the extremes of them be prime to one another, the last will not be to any other number as the first to the second.
heath_proof: For let there be as many numbers as we please, A, B, C, D, in continued proportion, and let the extremes of them, A, D, be prime to one another; I say that D is not to any other number as A is to B. For, if possible, as A is to B, so let D be to E; therefore, alternately, as A is to D, so is B to E. [VII. 13] But A, D are prime, primes are also least, [VII. 21] and the least numbers measure those which have the same ratio the same number of times, the antecedent the antecedent and the consequent the consequent. [VII. 20] Therefore A measures B. And, as A is to B, so is B to C. Therefore B also measures C; so that A also measures C. And since, as B is to C, so is C to D, and B measures C, therefore C also measures D. But A measured C; so that A also measures D. But it also measures itself; therefore A measures A, D which are prime to one another: which is impossible. Therefore D will not be to any other number as A is to B.
ai_proof_text:
9.17
**Statement:** If there be as many numbers as we please in continued proportion, and the extremes of them be prime to one another, the last will not be to any other number as the first to the second.

**Step 1.** Let A, B, C, D be as many numbers as we please in continued proportion, so that A : B = B : C = C : D, and let the extremes A, D be prime to one another. I say that D is not to any other number as A is to B.

**Step 2.** For, if possible, let A : B = D : E, where E is some number.

**Step 3.** Since the four numbers A, B, D, E are proportional, they are also proportional alternately [7.13]; therefore A : D = B : E.

**Step 4.** Since A, D are prime to one another, they are the least of the numbers which have the same ratio with them [7.21].

**Step 5.** The least numbers of those which have the same ratio with them measure those which have the same ratio the same number of times, the antecedent the antecedent and the consequent the consequent [7.20]. Since A : D = B : E and A, D are the least numbers in that ratio, A measures B.

**Step 6.** Since A measures B, A is a part of B [D7.3]. And A : B = B : C; but numbers are proportional when the first is the same part of the second that the third is of the fourth [D7.20]; therefore B is the same part of C that A is of B, so that B measures C [D7.3].

**Step 7.** Since A measures B and B measures C, A also measures C.

**Step 8.** Again, since B : C = C : D and B measures C, by the same reasoning as in Step 6, C measures D [D7.3, D7.20]. And A measures C; therefore A also measures D. In the same manner, however many the numbers in the continued proportion, A measures each of them in turn, and therefore measures the last, D.

**Step 9.** But A also measures itself. Therefore A, which is a number and not an unit [D7.2], measures both A and D, so that A, D have a number as a common measure. But A, D are prime to one another, that is, they are measured by an unit alone as a common measure [D7.12]: which is absurd.

**Step 10.** Therefore D is not to any other number as A is to B. Q.E.D.
